newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek brokers likely to adopt SMEHA proposals.
newsitem.headline: Greek brokers likely to adopt SMEHA proposals.

text.p: Greek stockbrokers met in a second emergency session to decide whether or not to adopt proposals to have trades by Delta Securities, now charged with fraud, and 10 other brokers nullified.
The second session of the day of the Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SEHMA) was in progress and it was still unclear if the bourse would open for trade on Tuesday.
"We're trying to adopt the proposals and, apparently, bourse President Manolis Xanthakis is likely to agree. It's pretty tense, but the real war will start after the clearing," a broker told Reuters.

SMEHA had proposed at an earlier session that trades with Delta Securities which took place from October 30 -- the trade date for which it issued bad cheques -- should be declared null. It suggested that the positions of all other members vis-a-vis the clearing house would be readjusted based on the decision to have the disputed trades with Delta reversed.

SMEHA has effectively stopped all trade on the bourse for two days, saying that, since Delta's default on 2.6 billion drachmas in settlements it was unclear whether or not they could count on payment for done deals.
SMEHA groups the 65 securities firms registered to trade on the Athens stock exchange. Settlement at the clearing house would be supervised by a three-member brokers' committee.
